text:
alex: Heads-up — after the landing of commit 4a5b6c we saw a 2-3x tail latency spike on the 8k seq workload. repro is simple: run the long-seq perf harness with batcher=adaptive + kv-cache enabled. :warning:

priya: Ack, saw alerts. Which kernel is blowing up?

alex: nsys trace points to a lot more time in the batcher scheduling path and a new kernel choice for the attention hotpath. Top items from quick nsys summary:
- attention_fwd_kernel: 42% -> 61% of GPU time
- batch_scheduler_spin and affinity_routing (device-side): up 3x
- kv_lookup async stalls increased, hit-rate seemed to drop

mike: Can you paste the nsys command you used? I'll run it locally.

alex: Sure:```bash
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --time-unit=ns -o /tmp/run-1768888888 \
  --sample=none ./runtime_perf_test --model long-seq --batches 5000
```
Then `nsys stats` -> report. trace uploaded: https://files.redwood.local/nsys/1768888888-run.nsys

jenna: I opened the trace — there's a clear gap where the batcher stalls waiting for KV callbacks, then falls back to a conservative kernel variant with higher thread-block count. The fallback appears to happen after the scheduler prefers affinity groups.

priya: That matches my local run. I also ran an nvprof slice. The statistic that jumped was CUDA API `cudaLaunchKernel` queuing latency for attention kernels.

perf-bot: automated snapshot: perfertto://traces/1768888888-ctx (viewable in perfetto UI)

mike: Could this be due to the recent hashing change in KV to improve locality? If the hashing skewed hot keys into different shards it could cause more async misses and evictions.

alex: I checked logs: before commit KV hit-rate ~98% for that workload, after commit it plummeted to ~64% in the same run. snippet from runtime logs:
```
[1768888891] KVCache: hits=4923 misses=276 miss_rate=5.3%  # pre-commit baseline
[1768888950] KVCache: hits=3180 misses=1808 miss_rate=36.3% # post-4a5b6c
```

jenna: Interesting — the miss pattern aligns with time windows where batcher picks smaller micro-batches and then selects the high-latency kernel. Might be an interaction: KV misses increase variance -> batcher sees higher stragglers -> scheduler switches kernel.

priya: Suggest we bisect between commits e1f2a3 (good) and 4a5b6c (bad) but narrow to changes touching kv hashing + batcher affinity. I'll start a `git bisect`. Steps I used:
```
git bisect start
git bisect bad 4a5b6c
git bisect good e1f2a3
# run the perf harness, check KV miss_rate > 20% to mark bad
```

mike: I'll automate a short triage job in CI that runs the harness for 200 batches and emits the KV hit/miss and a tiny nsys sample. If bisect points to the hashing patch, we can revert or tweak the bucket mapping.

alex: For quick local debugging try disabling affinity routing: set `batcher.prefer_affinity=false` in runtime config — that restored baseline for me in a smoke test. Not a fix but a useful mitigation.

jenna: I patched a local build toggling the hash seed back to the old value and retested: miss_rate drops to ~6% and tail latency normalizes. So likely culprit is the deterministic hash change.

priya: Good find. I'll complete the bisect and attach the exact commit that introduced the regression. Also capturing perfetto slices around the window to show kernel selection switching.

perf-bot: bisect status: started by priya, job id bisect-1768888888-1, link: https://ci.redwood.local/bisect/1768888888-1

alex: Thanks — once we have the exact commit I can prepare a rollback PR or a targeted fix: restore previous hashing or add KV warmup hints to batcher.

mike: I'll queue a canary with `batcher.prefer_affinity=false` and the new hashes to see if affinity toggle consistently mitigates.

jenna: Note for the patch: add a metric emitted by batcher about kernel_variant chosen per batch so we can correlate kernel flips with KV miss spikes going forward.

alex: Agreed. I'll open an issue with the trace links and add the mitigation PR. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

priya: follow-up: bisect ended — culprit commit 4a5b6c changed kv/hash.cc line 41-78. Opening PR to revert that chunk for now.
